notes: **Principle:** a GPS receiver calculates its position by measuring the time delay of radio signals from at least four satellites whose positions are known precisely.
**Satellite constellation:** 24+ satellites orbit at about 20,200 km altitude in six orbital planes, ensuring at least four are visible from any point on Earth at any time.
**Distance measurement:** distance = speed of light $\times$ time delay. A timing error of just 1 nanosecond causes a position error of about 30 cm.

**Relativistic corrections:** special relativity slows satellite clocks by about 7 microseconds/day due to their speed; general relativity speeds them up by about 45 microseconds/day due to weaker gravity at altitude. Net effect: +38 microseconds/day, which must be corrected or GPS would accumulate errors of about 10 km per day.
**Four satellites needed:** three give position in 3D space; the fourth gives the precise time, since the receiver's clock is not synchronized with satellite atomic clocks.
